import sympy as sp
x = sp.Symbol('x', positive=True)
k = sp.Symbol('k', integer=True, positive=True)
q = sp.Symbol('q', positive=True)
geom = sp.summation(q**k, (k, 1, sp.oo)).subs(q, sp.exp(-x))
assert sp.simplify(geom - 1 / (sp.exp(x) - 1)) == 0
term = sp.integrate(x**3 * sp.exp(-k * x), (x, 0, sp.oo))
assert sp.simplify(term - 6 / k**4) == 0
I_exact = sp.summation(term, (k, 1, sp.oo))
assert sp.simplify(I_exact - sp.pi**4 / 15) == 0
assert sp.simplify(6 * (sp.pi**4 / 90) - I_exact) == 0
print('geom_ok | term =', term, '| I_exact =', I_exact)

import mpmath as mp
mp.mp.dps = 65
I_quad = mp.quad(lambda u: u**3 / mp.expm1(u), [0, mp.inf])
I_closed = mp.pi**4 / 15
err = abs(I_quad - I_closed)
assert err < mp.mpf('1e-55')
print('I_quad   =', mp.nstr(I_quad, 52))
print('I_closed =', mp.nstr(I_closed, 52))
print('abs_err  =', mp.nstr(err, 6))

Separate 50-digit mpmath quadrature cross-check agrees with pi^4/15 to >55 digits (6.4939394022668291490960221792470074166485057115124).

On x in (0, infty), 0 < exp(-x) < 1, so x^3/(exp(x) - 1) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} x^3*exp(-k*x). Integrating term-by-term gives integral_0^{infty} x^3*exp(-k*x) dx = 6/k^4, and summing with the given zeta(4) = pi^4/90 yields:

I = pi^4/15

An independent 50-digit numerical quadrature cross-check confirms I = 6.4939394022668291490960221792470074166485057115124 (error < 1e-55).
